game: Week 3 HOU@IND / kickoff not saved / spread not saved / total not saved / weather not saved

script.base: Spread and total were not saved, so the script is inferred only from two-game form. Indianapolis has lived on Jonathan Taylor (43 carries, 190 yards) while Houston's run game has been stuck (David Montgomery 26 carries for 70 yards, 2.69 YPC; Woody Marks 17 for 50, 2.94 YPC) and C.J. Stroud has fed Dalton Schultz (22 targets, 175 yards, 130 air yards). Base case is a competitive game: IND keeps Taylor as the carry engine against a Houston run defense allowing 4.12 YPC, and Houston keeps throwing to Schultz into the middle, where Indianapolis allows 11.88 YPA.
script.flip1: Indianapolis gets ahead and leans further into Taylor clock work, so his rush-yard over survives, and Houston, already inefficient on the ground, abandons the run and funnels even more targets to Schultz.
script.flip2: Houston gets ahead, Indianapolis is forced off the Taylor run and onto Daniel Jones (EPA/dropback -0.22 with no blitz, and Houston blitzes only 17%), so Taylor's carries fall under what 81.5 needs; Houston can also finally run against a defense allowing 5.67 YPC, which would cut Schultz's target volume.

injury_fallout: MISSING: final injury report, practice status (DNP/limited/full), questionable tags, game-time decisions, and inactives for both HOU and IND, offense and defense. No absences, returns, or next-man-up inferred from usage.

matchup.shell: Coverage shell not in the pack (no MOFO/MOFC, no man/zone rate). IND blitzes 25% and allows 11.88 YPA middle (17 att) and 11.0 YPA left (22 att) versus 8.19 YPA right (32 att). HOU blitzes only 17% and allows 10.47 YPA middle (17 att) and 10.82 YPA right (28 att) versus 4.0 YPA left (15 att).
matchup.pressure: IND blitz rate 25%; Stroud EPA/dropback is +0.39 vs blitz (n=20) and -0.13 with no blitz, so Indianapolis pressure does not shut the Houston pass game down. HOU blitz rate 17%; Jones is -0.02 vs blitz (n=19) and -0.22 with no blitz, so he mostly sees the look he has been worse against.
matchup.bleeds: IND run defense bleeds: 5.67 YPC allowed and 10 runs of 10+ yards, plus 8 passes of 20+ on 75 attempts. HOU run defense is tighter (4.12 YPC, 5 runs of 10+) but the pass defense bleeds middle and right and has allowed 9 passes of 20+ on 68 attempts.
matchup.overlap: Houston's primary target is Dalton Schultz (22 targets, 175 yards, 130 air yards), and a TE attacks the middle, which is Indianapolis's worst pass location at 11.88 YPA. That is the clean overlap. Jonathan Taylor (43 carries, 190 yards) does not get a run-defense bleed — Houston allows only 4.12 YPC — so his case is carry share, not a soft front.

form: Only weeks 1-2 are in the pack, not a 3-4 game sample. Schultz is the Houston offense: 11 targets per game and 87.5 receiving yards per game, ahead of Hutchinson (15 targets, 69 yards, 169 air yards — opportunity without conversion), Collins (10/75/120), Noel (7/84/65, efficiency that may be one-play driven), Wayne (8/45/116) and Boutte (7/58/98). Montgomery leads Houston carries (26/70) over Marks (17/50) but neither has cleared 3.0 YPC. Taylor is a workhorse at 21.5 carries and 95 rush yards per game, plus 8 targets for 63 yards. Downs leads IND receivers (13/109/109); Warren has 12 targets but only 34 yards and 10 air yards; Allen 11/37/53.

edge_players.kills_it: IF Houston commits to the run against the IND defense that allows 5.67 YPC and Dalton Schultz draws fewer than 6 targets THEN Dalton Schultz receiving yards over 49.5 fails

market_rung_price: daltonschultz recyds over 49.5 at -114 (main line, no alt rung in pack); jonathantaylor rushyds over 81.5 at -114 (main line, no alt rung in pack). Neither is a short-priced alt.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Schultz's 87.5-yard pace was a two-game heater, Indianapolis took the middle away after 22 targets, and Houston finally ran against a defense allowing 5.67 YPC, so Schultz never saw a seventh target and finished under 49.5 — the -114 price already refused to buy the heater, and a late inactive not in this pack would explain the number. Taylor faced a Houston front that has allowed only 5 runs of 10+ yards and 4.12 YPC, Houston led, Indianapolis threw, and 15 carries at that efficiency landed in the mid-60s, short of 81.5. That counter is real on Taylor because the run defense is not a bleed and the spread is unknown, so he stays a lean; it is not stronger than the Schultz read, whose role and the middle bleed both point over.
slip_story: One story: competitive game or Indianapolis controls the lead. Taylor rush yards over is the IND run-control leg; Schultz receiving yards over is Houston answering through the middle whether the game is close or Houston is chasing. They co-hit in the base script and in the IND-leads flip. Do not add Houston RB overs, which need Houston to run against the 5.67 YPC defense, or Indianapolis receiver overs that need Jones in a pass-heavy chase — those belong to the other flip.
